There aren't that many people here, so I figure it's worth using that to our advantage. Please take the time to write up something so we can get to know each other or get a background on posters.
What does your program look like, how long have you been doing it, and do you recommend it to someone with similar experience to yourself?

I'm male, 5'9, 26 years old. 169lbs.

I started lifting after I dislocated my shoulder and the doctors told me muscle would help keep it in. I had lifted in high school for wrestling, but I had a high schooler's mind then. I also wanted a body that is admired, so I began. Of course I did the one body part a week thing. 3X8s without any real plan. I did go up in weight (noob gains), and did get in pretty good shape. At that point I was still convinced I could lose fat and gain muscle.

Although I put in a lot of work, I ended up dislocating my shoulder again while rock climbing, so I was basically back to square 1. I found the fitness reddit, and started realizing that cutting/bulking are generally more efficient. I switched between 3X5s and 3X8's depending on if I stalled at one or the other. After 2 years of that, I started PPL routine because I realized I could work out muscles twice a week and not be too tired. Right now I do a personal PPL(and shoulders) routine that looks like this.

FYI I'm cutting for summer

Then I do biceps on this day.

Seated isolation curls: 3X10

Machine hammer curl 3X12

Abs

I do these whenever they're not tired along with calves between the circuit.

Circuit 3X

Standing ab wheel: X8

Seated Mason twists with balls; X20

Crunch machine: 3X10.

I'm eating 1500 calories a day and losing 1.2 pounds a week on average. I don't think I'd recommend the program because it's a lot of volume and tough to stay consistent through the week. For some reason I feel like I'm losing out if I don't do all those exercises (even though I could probably sub out a few). Four day splits are tough and I usually end up not taking enough time off, or losing out on another workout because I'm not recovered enough.
